metadata.case_name: LIU CHEUNG KEUNG v. NG CHI KEUNG

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: transport worker, warehouse worker, car park attendant, cleaner, watchman, cashier, factory worker, masseur and porter

injuries.description: ruptured left eyeball with linear full thickness corneo-scleral laceration
source: ruptured left eyeball with linear full thickness corneo-scleral laceration
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: distorted iris of the left eye
source: distorted iris of the left eye

injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral
Contusion of eyeball or orbital tissues

injuries.description: suspicious foreign body was seen in the left eyeball
source: Suspicious foreign body was seen in the left eyeball.
injuries.icd_description: Retained foreign body following penetrating wound of orbit

injuries.description: pseudophakic left eye (crystalline lens removed and replaced by an intraocular lens)
source: The Plaintiff’s left eye is pseudophakic (i.e. the crystalline lens had been removed by surgery and replaced by an intraocular lens).

manifestations.description: visual acuity of the left eye was hand movement
best corrected visual acuity of the left eye was 20/200
occasional pain and discomfort in left eye
double image; reliance on right eye for reading; right eye gets tired easily
total loss of accommodation resulting in very poor vision for reading and close work
pupil abnormalities with a slightly dilated pupil
pain and discomfort caused by the displacement or protrusion of the stitches after the surgery
The overall permanent visual impairment in the Plaintiff’s left eye is assessed to be 70%

treatments_received: Emergency operation to repair the ruptured eyeball (26 April 2005)
Hospital treatment at Accident and Emergency Department, Princess Margaret Hospital (immediate post-accident)
Transfer and follow-up treatment at Caritas Medical Eye Unit / Caritas Medical Centre
Cataract extraction and implantation of intraocular lens (22 September 2005)
Removal/trimming of protruded stitches on 8 occasions
treatments_future: No further treatment required (Dr. Paul Cheung opinion)

losses.description: Failure to enjoy a normal life because of impaired vision in the left eye, including blurring of vision, discomfort and reduced ability to read and close work.
Pain and discomfort caused by protruding stitches remaining in the left eye after surgery (stitches sometimes displaced or protruded).

comparable_cases.case_name: Sze Ping Chui v Lau Ching Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: Ruptured eyeball on left eye with a 5 mm full thickness linear corneal laceration at the visual axis; lens damaged; urgent operations to repair the cornea, remove damaged lens and implant intra-ocular lens; residual corneal scar; blurred vision, occasional "light reflection", discomfort and photophobia; myopia and severe astigmatism; pseudophakic condition; visual acuity assessed at 35%; permanent disability assessed at 67%.
